editorial:
Imagine you are a stressed-out grad student just trying to finish your degree, and you suddenly find yourself pretending to date the meanest professor on campus. That is exactly what happens to Olive, a biology student who accidentally kisses Dr. Adam Carlsen to prove a point to her friend. Adam agrees to the fake relationship because it helps him with his job, but the two of them couldn't be more different. He is a grumpy genius, and she is a nervous wreck. The whole vibe is super cute and funny, feeling like a warm hug of a movie that doesn't take itself too seriously. You will love watching their awkward chemistry grow as they try to follow their own rules about love.

The acting is great, and the pacing keeps you interested without feeling rushed. While some of the plot points are a bit predictable, the sweet moments make up for it. If you love stories where opposites attract, you need to see this.
endingExplained: After a big misunderstanding about their feelings, Olive and Adam finally stop pretending. Adam admits that he actually fell in love with her long before the fake dating started. They have a heartfelt talk where they clear up all the lies and decide to be a real couple. The movie ends with them happily together, balancing their professional lives and their new romance, proving that love is the one thing you cannot plan with a theory.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fake dating tropes and cute academic settings.
similarMovies: To All the Boys I've Loved Before
